clue.text: Keep part of it as a fortified building

definitions.text: Keep part of it as a fortified building

parts.words: Keep part of it as a fortified building
parts.note: the keep is the central tower of a medieval stronghold, so the clue describes a fortress whose keep is one part

explanation.surface: Someone is advised to preserve a portion of something as a fort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' reads as a verb meaning preserve, but it is the noun: the strong inner tower of a medieval fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval stronghold with walls and towers is a fortified building, and its keep is its innermost tower.

clue.text: Padre has tea without milk and sugar?

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
tea served with nothing added is plain

explanation.surface: A priest takes his tea black and unsweetened.
explanation.walkthrough: CHA is old British slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A padre is a military or institutional clergyman, a chaplain.

clue.text: Might be the alcohol content

definitions.meaning: might as a noun means power or force
the proportion of alcohol in a drink, how potent it is

explanation.surface: Someone guesses at how boozy a drink is.
explanation.definitionFit: Might is physical power; a drink's potency is measured by its proof.

clue.text: Whip has turned on beginner

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting one piece on another places it below, so it comes second

parts.note: L is the learner plate worn by a beginner driver in Britain

indicators.note: turned means the letters of has are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: A whip has been turned against a novice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' rearranges HAS to ASH, which sits 'on' (below, in a down clue) L, the British learner-driver symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: To flog someone is to whip them with strokes.

clue.text: Stand face to face with many on the promenade

indicators.note: in an across clue 'on' here means the first piece comes before the second

parts.note: a con, short for convict, is a man in prison
the front is a seaside promenade in British resorts

explanation.surface: Someone meets a man head-on during a stroll along the seafront.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'many' must be 'man': CON (convict) put before FRONT. In British seaside towns 'the front' is the promenade along the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To challenge someone directly is to stand opposite them, face to face.

clue.text: Responding more violently than is justified concerning catering arrangements

definitions.text: Responding more violently than is justified

parts.note: over can mean concerning, as in a row over money

indicators.note: arrangements suggests the letters of catering are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone flies off the handle about the food plans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrangements' turns CATERING into REACTING, placed after OVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Making too much of something, responding with excessive force, is a disproportionate response.

clue.text: Flatter colour

definitions.meaning: to flatter servilely, crawling to win favour
a pale yellowish-brown shade, like a young deer

explanation.surface: A more even shade of paint.
explanation.definitionFit: To grovel for favour is to toady; a light greyish-brown is a shade named after a young deer.

clue.text: Offer more in an attempt to take the lot

definitions.text: Offer more in an attempt to take the lot

parts.words: Offer more in an attempt to take the lot
parts.note: describes an auction bidder topping a rival's price to win the item for sale

explanation.surface: A buyer at auction raises their bid to win the item.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'lot' is an item for sale at an auction.
explanation.definitionFit: At an auction, offering a higher price than a rival in order to win the item is overbidding them.

clue.text: Black and brown plaid

parts.note: tar is black
tan is a brown colour

explanation.surface: A dark-coloured woollen fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: A tartan is the checked woollen cloth of a Scottish clan.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaid is the patterned Scottish cloth with crossing coloured stripes.

clue.text: Stop for a break, say

indicators.note: 'say' asks for the words a break to be spoken, giving a sound shared with another word

parts.note: a rest is a break from work

explanation.surface: A request to halt for a breather.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'a rest' (a break) sounds like the word meaning to stop someone, as police do.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt or check movement, as police halt a suspect, is to stop it.

clue.text: Various wet areas contain it

indicators.note: various suggests the letters of wet areas are put into a different order

explanation.surface: Oceans and other soggy regions are full of a liquid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Various' rearranges WETAREAS; the whole clue is also the definition, since oceans and seas are filled with salt water.
explanation.definitionFit: Oceans and other marine regions, wet areas indeed, are filled with saline liquid from the ocean.

clue.text: Even this accommodation is below ground

indicators.note: is here links the two pieces, the level word joined to the underground storey

parts.note: a basement is the storey below ground level
even means level, which is flat

explanation.surface: Even this home is underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Even' reads as 'indeed', but it means level, FLAT; BASEMENT (below ground) comes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An apartment on the lowest, underground storey of a house is a form of accommodation.

clue.text: Come down to earth

definitions.meaning: to come down from the air, as an aircraft does onto a runway
earth in the sense of ground or soil, a plot of terrain

explanation.surface: Someone is told to stop daydreaming and be realistic.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft touching down comes down, and ground or terrain is the soil of earth.

clue.text: Transport vehicle by rail

parts.note: a car is a road vehicle
RY is an abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A car is shipped by train.
explanation.definitionFit: To transport goods is to convey or bear them from place to place.

clue.text: The tower here is inclined to attract visitors

definitions.text: The tower here is inclined to attract visitors

parts.words: The tower here is inclined to attract visitors
parts.note: describes an Italian city whose famous bell tower leans, drawing tourists

explanation.surface: A tower seems eager to draw in tourists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inclined' reads as willing, but it means leaning: the city in Tuscany famous for its leaning bell tower.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tuscan city is home to the famous leaning campanile, which tourists flock to see.

clue.text: Race in which Bert and I perform

indicators.note: perform suggests the letters of Bert and I are worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: Two friends put on an act in a running event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Race' reads as a contest, but it means a people or clan; 'perform' rearranges BERT and I.
explanation.definitionFit: A race in the old sense of a people of common descent is a clan or people.

clue.text: Discourage this man as a cleaner

indicators.note: this points at the answer: the answer with a man added makes a cleaner, so the man is taken off the cleaner

parts.note: detergent is a cleaning agent
a gent is a man

explanation.surface: Someone tries to put a man off working as a cleaner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This' is the answer itself: this plus 'man' (GENT) is a cleaner, DETERGENT, so remove GENT to leave the word meaning discourage.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone off from acting is to discourage them.

clue.text: Deceased buried without being mutually connected

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for buried goes around the other piece

parts.note: interred means buried
late means deceased, as in 'the late king'

explanation.surface: A dead person is buried alone, unconnected to anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' is the old sense 'outside': LATE goes inside INTERRED, between INTERRE and D.
explanation.definitionFit: Things linked to each other reciprocally are joined in a two-way relation.

clue.text: Lily hopes lad will become excited

indicators.note: excited suggests the letters of hopes lad are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Lily hopes a young man will get worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lily' reads as a girl's name, but it is the flower: a plant of the lily family.
explanation.definitionFit: The asphodel is a flowering plant of the lily family, linked in myth with the Elysian fields.

clue.text: Intuitive power this month in court

parts.note: inst., short for instant, means this month in old business letters

explanation.surface: Gut feeling is tested in a courtroom this month.
explanation.walkthrough: INST (instant) was once used in commercial letters for 'of this month', as in 'your letter of the 5th inst.'
explanation.definitionFit: An innate gut feeling that acts without reasoning is an intuitive power.

clue.text: Make fewer complaints about a practical demonstration

parts.note: to object less is to protest or complain less often
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to grumble less regarding a hands-on display.
explanation.definitionFit: A lesson taught by showing a real example is a hands-on demonstration of the principle.

clue.text: Make a great effort to filter through

definitions.meaning: to exert oneself hard, pushing to the limit
to pass a liquid through a sieve or cloth to remove solids

explanation.surface: Someone works hard to pass a liquid through a sieve.
explanation.definitionFit: To exert oneself is to toil hard; pouring liquid through a sieve separates out the solids.

clue.text: Two boys shortly will become the target

parts.note: Vic is short for the boy's name Victor
Tim is short for the boy's name Timothy

explanation.surface: A pair of lads will soon be singled out for attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortly' reads as soon, but it means the boys' names are shortened forms.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone singled out for attack or abuse is a target, the one harmed.

clue.text: Cotton on a thin stick

definitions.meaning: to cotton on is informal for to understand or realise
a small slender shoot of a tree

explanation.surface: Thread is wound around a slender stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, to grasp something suddenly is to cotton on; a small slender branch is a thin stick.

clue.text: Make amends before two o'clock

definitions.meaning: to make up for a wrong one has done
the phrase ... names a time an hour before two

explanation.surface: Someone must apologise ahead of an afternoon deadline.
explanation.definitionFit: To expiate a wrong is to make amends; read as two words, it gives the time 1pm, just before two.

clue.text: Card game that's pointless for a bit

indicators.note: pointless says a compass point, S for south, is dropped from the card game

parts.note: whist is a trick-taking card game

explanation.surface: A card game played with no scoring, just for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pointless' looks like 'without scoring', but it drops a compass point, S (south), from WHIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny amount, as in 'not a whit', is a little bit.

clue.text: Metal golf club

definitions.meaning: a strong grey metallic element, Fe
a golf club with an angled metal head, numbered by loft

explanation.surface: A golf club made of metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Fe is a common metallic element; golfers use numbered clubs with angled metal heads.

clue.text: Pass a soft drink

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass

explanation.surface: Someone hands over a fizzy drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass' reads as hand over, but it is a col, a pass between mountain peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet fizzy carbonated beverage flavoured with kola nut is a soft drink.

clue.text: Despite everything is last

definitions.meaning: a phrase meaning in spite of all that has happened
something coming behind every other one is the last

explanation.surface: Someone insists that, regardless, something comes at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as one phrase it means nevertheless; read as two words, coming behind every other thing means being last.

clue.text: Dull court room

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them
a den is a small private room

explanation.surface: A tedious courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court room' reads as a law court, but 'court' is the verb meaning to woo, and 'room' is a den.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiff, lifeless performance is dull and expressionless.

clue.text: Mention a different name

indicators.note: different asks for the letters of mention a in another order

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to call something by another title.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone forward for a post is to name them as a candidate.

clue.text: Vote to come back after the dance

indicators.note: after places the reversed piece behind the dance

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

indicators.note: come back signals the little word to is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to return after the dance to cast a vote.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret poll in which electors choose is a vote.
